title: This Is What Gets In The Way
author: Brainard Carey

spans.text: Life comes at you fast. It doesn’t matter if you have plans made or goals to reach, the demands of the day-to-day don’t quit, and sometimes they go into overdrive without warning. Staying focused can feel next to impossible at times, and there are some instances when the only sensible option is to take a step back and give yourself some needed space. But when your career is on the line, as is often the case for artists, how might you continue nurturing that even when chaos swirls all around you? Taking small steps is often the answer. Submit a small number of applications to opportunities that might work for you in the future, take five minutes to do a little searching around for upcoming deadlines. No matter how small, all forward motion is a good thing.

spans.text: The art world is for you. It is for everyone, viewer and artist alike. While it may feel difficult to break in, the art world in fact needs artists just as much as artists need the art world. Without creators, there simply is no art. The challenge is finding those ways to sustain and grow your practice so you can continue to make inroads toward the career you desire. Here are some upcoming opportunities to keep you on the right track.

spans.text: Sometimes life asks more of us than others, not because we have everything figured out, but because someone else needs us to show up. In difficult moments, when uncertainty, loss, change, or simply the weight of the world has you feeling stretched thin, it can be tempting to turn inward. But these can be the moments when coming through for one another matters most.

title: Got To Roll With The Punches
author: Brainard Carey

spans.text: Sometimes life can throw us curveballs. When things seem to be chugging along, progress happening, out of nowhere we get hit with an obstacle that knocks us down for bit. It happens to everybody at some time or another, and while it can be demoralizing to feel like you’ve been thrown off course, you can and will regain your footing. For artists, this can feel like a particularly existential threat, putting a hard built career in jeopardy. But there are always more opportunities out there, and even when you’re down and out, hope lingers on the horizon.

At times it can feel like everyone else is getting the exhibition, the grant, the residency, or the attention you’ve been working toward. Building an art career is rarely a straight line, rather it’s a process of showing up, continuing to make work that matters to you, and staying connected to opportunities that can move your practice forward. Every application you submit, every new resource you discover, and every connection you make adds another piece to the foundation you’re building.
